q: 1. The expenses of items which do not come under any regular head of items and the cost of unforeseen items are called
explain: Contingencies represent incidental expenses of a miscellaneous character that cannot be reasonably predicted during the estimation stage.

q: 2. The value of the property (without being dismantled) at the end of the useful life period is known as
explain: Salvage (or salvation) value is the value of the property at the end of its life without being dismantled. If dismantled, it is called scrap value.

q: 3. Actual cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor. Such a contract is known as
explain: In a 'Cost Plus Percentage' contract, the owner pays the contractor the actual expenses incurred plus a fixed percentage for profit and overhead.

q: 4. The annual periodic payments made for the repayment of the capital invested in known a
explain: Annuity refers to a fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, typically for the rest of their life or to repay capital.

q: 5. The value of the dismantled material less the cost of dismantling is called
explain: Scrap value is the worth of the materials (bricks, steel, timber) after a building is demolished, minus the labor cost of demolition.

q: 6. The value of the property (without being dismantled) at the end of the useful life period is known as
explain: Salvage value is the estimated value of an asset at the end of its useful life without being dismantled. If the asset is dismantled and sold as material, it is called scrap value.

q: 7. The gradual accumulation of amount by way of annual periodic deposits which is meant for the replacement of the structure at the end of its useful life period is known as
explain: A sinking fund is created by setting aside a small amount of money every year so that at the end of the building's life, the accumulated amount is enough to rebuild or replace the structure.

q: 8. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed by the department to complete the work at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is hired to finish a defaulted contract, and the costs incurred are debited (charged) from the original contractor's pending bills or security deposit.

q: 9. The life of brick work work is generally assumed to
explain: First-class brickwork in cement mortar is considered highly durable and is usually assigned a useful life of 100 years in valuation.

q: 10. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: Major sanitary items are typically estimated as 'sets' which include the primary fixture plus all necessary brackets, pipes, and fixing labor.

q: 11. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: Items like sinks, WCs, and basins are 'by number' items, and their rate includes the cost of the unit and its installation.

q: 12. If the payment of annuity begins after some years in future, it is known as
explain: A deferred annuity is a type of annuity contract that delays payments until the investor chooses to receive them in the future.

q: 13. Annual rent is generally fixed at
explain: In valuation, the gross annual rent of a property is typically estimated between 5% to 10% of the total capital cost of the building.

q: 14. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than .....% of the capital cost.
explain: To ensure economic maintenance, repair costs are generally capped at 2.5% of the original capital cost of the building per year.

q: 15. When a contractor is paid certain percentage over the actual cost of the construction as his profit, such contract is termed as
explain: In a 'Cost Plus Percentage' contract, the contractor is reimbursed for all actual expenses plus an agreed-upon percentage of those costs as profit.

q: 16. Annual rent is generally fixed at
explain: For valuation purposes, the annual rent of a property is generally estimated between 5% and 10% of the total capital cost of the building.

q: 17. Original cost of property minus deprecation is
explain: Book Value is the amount shown in the account books after deducting the total depreciation from the original cost of the asset.

q: 18. The valuation of a building depends upon
explain: Building valuation is influenced by technical factors like material quality and structural integrity, as well as functional factors like size and design.

q: 19. The total estimated cost of a building electrification usually accounts for
explain: Standard estimating norms typically allocate approximately 8% of the total building cost for internal electrical installations.

q: 20. The valuation of property is done when
options: owner of the property wants to sell it
municipal tax... have to be fixed
insurance of the property has to be done
explain: Valuation is required for various purposes including buying/selling, taxation assessment, insurance coverage, and mortgage security.

q: 21. The value of property that can be obtained at any particular time from the open market if the property is put for sale, is known as
explain: Market value is the estimated amount for which an asset should exchange on the date of valuation between a willing buyer and a willing seller.

q: 22. The amount of annuity paid at the beginning of each year and continued to pay for the definite number of periods known as:
explain: When payments are made at the beginning of each period, it is technically an 'annuity due', though the answer key identifies 'annuity value' in this specific context.

q: 23. The sinking fund is:
options: a part of the proceed in reserve for additional structure...
the sum of money to be paid to authorities by the tenants
the fund for rebuilding a structure when its economic life is over.
raised to meet the maintenance costs...
explain: A sinking fund is a fund created by periodically setting aside money so that the total amount at the end of the building's life equals the cost of replacement.

q: 24. The value of structure without being dismantled at the end of its utility period is known as:
explain: Salvage value is the estimated resale value of an asset at the end of its useful life, assuming the asset is sold whole and not broken up into materials.

q: 25. The set annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deduction the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
explain: Rateable value is the net annual income of a property used by local authorities to calculate municipal taxes.

q: 26. The term 'valuation' in reference to Civil Engineering is the process of estimating the potential .......of an asset.
explain: Valuation is primarily used to determine the 'fair' value (book or market) of a property for legal, financial, or accounting purposes.

q: 27. Commonly adopted method of building valuation by commercial bank is basically based on
explain: Banks often use the plinth area method for quick valuation as it provides a reliable market-standard assessment based on the total built-up area of the property.

q: 28. As compared to capital cost, the total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than
explain: Standard maintenance budgeting limits the annual and special repair costs to 2.5% of the total construction cost.

q: 29. The loss of value of property by its becoming out of date in style, in design, in structure etc, is called as
explain: Obsolescence occurs when a property loses value because its design or technology is no longer preferred by the market, even if it is physically sound.

q: 30. As compared to total cost of construction of a building, scarp value is taken as
explain: Scrap value (the value of materials after dismantling) is generally estimated at 10% of the original construction cost.

q: 31. The life of teakwood doors and windows is usually taken
explain: While teak is highly durable, for valuation and depreciation purposes, its service life is typically estimated at 40 years.

q: 32. Which of following is corrected?
explain: Depending on the type of asset and its condition at the end of its utility period, the salvage value (value without dismantling) can be higher, lower, or equal to the scrap value (value of dismantled materials).

q: 33. The decrease in the value of the property due to structural deterioration, continuous use, wear and tear, decay and obsolescence is termed as ............
explain: Depreciation is the gradual reduction in the value of an asset over time due to age, wear, or becoming outdated.
